page: Amazon Web Services c7gn.large is a compute-optimized instance powered by custom AWS Graviton processors. Built on the 64-bit ARM architecture using the ARMv8 Neoverse-V1 core model, this server features 2 dedicated physical cores running at 2.6 GHz with a 1.0 thread-per-core ratio. The CPU configuration includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It is equipped with 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The instance operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, lacks local storage, and does not include any GPU accelerators.

Performance benchmarks reveal a mix of average and weaker results. Single-core performance is a relative strength, with the stress-ng single-core CPU test and Geekbench single-core score both falling into the average category. Single-threaded tasks like gzip compression and bzip3 decompression also show average performance. However, multi-core and multi-threaded benchmarks, such as stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression, register as weak or poor, reflecting the constraints of its 2-core configuration. Memory bandwidth read-only large block performance is average at 57.94 GB/sec, whereas write performance and small-block read performance are weaker.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c7gn.large offers a resource-dense entry point for ARM-based deployments, trading off raw multi-threaded performance for dedicated core execution and high network throughput. It features a baseline network bandwidth of 6 Gbps and is optimized for EBS. This profile makes the instance suitable for lightweight network-bound workloads, single-threaded application servers, basic web serving, and software compilation tasks that do not require massive parallel processing or local storage.
description: Amazon Web Services c7gn.large is a compute-optimized, ARM64-based instance powered by AWS Graviton Neoverse-V1 processors. Running on the Nitro hypervisor, it features 2 dedicated physical cores at 2.6 GHz, 4.0 GB of memory, and a baseline network bandwidth of 6 Gbps, with no local storage or GPU hardware. Benchmarks indicate average single-core CPU performance and single-threaded compression speeds, though multi-core and multi-threaded workloads show weaker results due to the dual-core constraint. This server represents a qualitatively cost-efficient entry point for ARM architecture development, offering dedicated compute resources without the overhead of larger instances. It is best suited for lightweight network-bound applications, single-threaded processing, basic web serving, and software compilation.
